title: Admin command graph sandboxifier for safe runbook experimentation
creator: Alex R. Chen
description: Build a lightweight 'sandboxifier' that compiles admin runbooks and ad-hoc operator sequences into an executable command graph that can be safely dry-run, validated, and replayed in an isolated environment. The goal is to let SREs and support engineers iterate on runbook changes, test permission/effect assumptions, and gather deterministic telemetry before committing changes to production playbooks. This work touches admin utilities, runbooks-as-tasks, and support automation surface area: command translation, idempotency checks, credential scoping, and replay telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Command graph compiler converts >90% of existing runbook step primitives to graph nodes without manual edits. 2) Dry-run mode exercises the graph in an isolated sandbox (no external writes) and produces a deterministic trace. 3) Permission gating enforces least-privilege via ephemeral scoped credentials (STS) for sandbox runs. 4) Safety hooks allow aborts on resource modification heuristics and provide clear operator signals. 5) Integration tests (unit + e2e) added to CI demonstrating a canary flow against a synthetic tenant.

design_decisions: Interpret-then-compile approach chosen (parse -> normalize -> compile) to allow future optimizations and easier annotations for safety.
Prefer read-only simulation via client shims over full virtualization to reduce infra cost for sandbox runs.
Expose a 'confidence' metric for each compiled node to indicate how closely the simulator mirrors production behavior (used in canary gating).
tradeoffs: Compiler complexity vs flexibility: compiling to a DAG enables analyses (idempotency, parallelism) but requires keeping translators for many primitives.
Simulation fidelity vs cost: deeper fidelity requires full mock environments which are expensive; we start with shim-based simulation and add targeted mocks for high-risk primitives.
Signal surface: adding more telemetry increases visibility but also ingest cost; initial telemetry set is minimal and will be expanded based on incident learnings.
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for parser/normalizer/compiler (aim >= 90% coverage for core modules). e2e tests run against a synthetic tenant cluster (read-only mode) on CI that validates trace determinism. Chaos test: introduce API latency and ensure dry-run still produces deterministic trace and aborts on heuristics. Manual runbook authoring session with Support team to validate UX and failure modes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'sandboxifier.alpha' for admin accounts. 2) Internal beta with SRE + Oncall for 2 weeks monitoring telemetry for false positives/negatives. 3) Gradual enablement to Support org with training doc and runbook migration guide. 4) Gate full rollout on security signoff and observed <1% false negative change detection rate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Simulator diverges from production behavior leading to false confidence. Mitigation: Keep confidence metric and require small live canary runs for high-risk playbooks.
Risk: Privilege escalation if sandbox obtains broader creds. Mitigation: Ephemeral scoped STS tokens, strict IAM policies, and audit logs for all sandbox runs.
Risk: Tooling complexity slows adoption. Mitigation: Prioritize developer ergonomics, clear CLI/console UX, and migration scripts for existing runbooks.
